questions.question: Sami receives a patient with severe maxillary bone atrophy. He says: 'We can place short implants or do a sinus lift.' Mina, more cautious, asks: 'What is the main risk of the sinus lift?'
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Perforation of the sinus membrane is the most common complication of the sinus lift.' Sami, reassured, prepares for the procedure.

questions.question: Mina, planning a sinus lift, explains the lateral window technique to Sami. Sami asks: 'When do we use this technique?'
options: When a large amount of bone is needed to place long implants
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The lateral window is indicated for large bone defects.' Sami, taking notes, observes the procedure.

questions.question: Sami, looking at an X-ray, asks Mina: 'What is a short implant?' Mina replies:
options: An implant less than 8mm in length
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Short implants are an alternative to bone grafts.' Sami, surprised, learns about this option.

questions.question: Mina, analyzing a case, tells Sami: 'Be careful of the proximity to the sinus!' Sami asks: 'Why is it a risk?'
options: Risk of oro-sinusal communication and infection
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Communication with the sinus can lead to infections.' Sami, cautious, takes precautions.

questions.question: Sami, placing an implant in the mandible, asks Mina: 'How to avoid damaging the inferior alveolar nerve?' Mina replies:
options: By respecting a safety distance of 2mm on the CBCT
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The CBCT allows precise measurement of the distance.' Sami, focused, checks every measurement.

questions.question: Mina, placing an implant, tells Sami: 'I use a surgical guide for more precision.' Sami asks: 'What are the advantages of the guide?'
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The guide allows precise and safe placement.' Sami, admiring, wishes to use one.

questions.question: Sami, after placing an implant, notices mobility. Mina tells him: 'It's a failure of primary stability.' Sami asks: 'What are the causes?'
options: Poor bone quality, too wide drilling, infection
Too dense bone, too slow drilling
Implant too long, crown too heavy
Patient too young, diet too hard
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Failure of primary stability can be due to several factors.' Sami, disappointed, must remove the implant.

questions.question: Mina, reassessing a patient, tells Sami: 'There is peri-implantitis.' Sami asks: 'What causes it?'
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Peri-implantitis is caused by bacteria and insufficient hygiene.' Sami, worried, asks how to treat it.

questions.question: Sami asks Mina how to treat peri-implantitis. Mina replies:
options: Mechanical debridement, disinfection, sometimes regenerative surgery
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Treatment is complex and requires a multidisciplinary approach.' Sami, attentive, follows her advice.

questions.question: Mina, talking about immediate loading, tells Sami: 'A high insertion torque is required.' Sami asks: 'Why is that important?'
options: High primary stability is necessary to support immediate loading
To make the implant more aesthetic
To reduce pain for the patient
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Primary stability is the key criterion for immediate loading.' Sami, understanding, checks the torque.

questions.question: Sami, seeing an implant with an incorrect angle, asks Mina: 'Should it be removed?' Mina replies:
options: Not necessarily, you can sometimes use an angled abutment
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Angled abutments can correct axis defects.' Sami, relieved, learns this trick.

questions.question: Mina, preparing a case, tells Sami: 'We must choose the right implant diameter.' Sami asks: 'How do we choose it?'
options: Based on the available bone width
Based on the price of the implant
Based on the color of the gum
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The diameter must be adapted to the bone width.' Sami, taking notes, measures carefully.

questions.question: Sami, at the end of treatment, asks Mina: 'When should the definitive loading be done?' Mina replies:
options: After 3 to 6 months, depending on bone quality
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The delay varies depending on bone quality.' Sami, patient, waits for the right moment.

questions.question: Mina, analyzing a failure, tells Sami: 'Failure can be early or late.' Sami asks: 'What is an early failure?'
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Early failure occurs before loading.' Sami, slightly disappointed, analyzes the causes.

questions.question: Sami asks Mina: 'What are the causes of late failure?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Late failures are often due to long-term problems.' Sami, taking notes, is more vigilant.

questions.question: Mina, talking about materials, tells Sami: 'There are zirconium implants.' Sami asks: 'What is their advantage?'
options: Better aesthetics and absence of metal
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Zirconium is more aesthetic and non-metallic.' Sami, interested, promises to look into it.

questions.question: Sami, looking at an X-ray, asks Mina: 'What is an onlay bone graft?' Mina replies:
options: A graft placed on the bone surface to increase its volume
A graft placed inside the bone
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The onlay graft is a technique to increase bone volume.' Sami, fascinated, observes the technique.

questions.question: Mina, explaining a case, tells Sami: 'Sometimes we need to do a block graft.' Sami asks: 'What is it?'
options: A bone graft harvested in block and fixed with screws
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The block graft is used for large defects.' Sami, admiring, observes the procedure.

questions.question: Sami, after a graft, asks Mina: 'How long should we wait before placing the implant?' Mina replies:
options: 4 to 6 months, the time for graft consolidation
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'We must allow time for the graft to consolidate.' Sami, patient, waits for the right moment.

questions.question: Mina, talking about complications, tells Sami: 'Implant fracture is rare.' Sami asks: 'What can cause it?'
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Fractures are often due to excessive forces.' Sami, cautious, checks the occlusion.

questions.question: Sami, talking with a patient, asks Mina: 'What are the warning signs after implant placement?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'These signs should alert the patient.' Sami, conscientious, explains them to the patient.

questions.question: Mina, analyzing a case, tells Sami: 'Maintenance is crucial in implantology.' Sami asks: 'What does it involve?'
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Maintenance is essential for the longevity of the implant.' Sami, understanding, plans follow-up.

questions.question: Sami, looking at a follow-up X-ray, asks Mina: 'What is an acceptable marginal bone loss?' Mina replies:
options: Less than 1.5mm in the first year, then less than 0.2mm per year
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Physiological bone loss is normal within certain limits.' Sami, reassured, validates the results.

questions.question: Mina, at the end of treatment, tells Sami: 'Long-term success depends on several factors.' Sami asks: 'Which ones?'
options: Bone quality, hygiene, occlusion, prosthetic design
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'All these factors influence the longevity of implants.' Sami, aware, promises to be rigorous.

questions.question: Sami, seeing the final result, tells Mina: 'It's a success!' Mina replies: 'Success is measured in the long term.' Sami, understanding, promises to follow his patients long-term.
options: Success in implantology is measured in the long term
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Longevity is the true criterion of success.' Sami, convinced, adopts this philosophy.
